channel.title: Mapping Forward
channel.description: Daily synthesis of articles on cartography, mapping, geospatial data, and geographic intelligence

item.title: Volcanic Eruption Map Spotlight: Anak Krakatau, Indonesia
item.description: Anak Krakatau volcano in Indonesia's Sunda Strait erupted on September 4, 2026, sending ash plumes to 50,000 feet, disrupting 300+ flights, and prompting evacuation zones and air quality monitoring via interactive maps. — Key takeaways: Anak Krakatau began erupting on September 4, 2026, producing lava fountains and ash plumes reaching approximately 50,000 feet ; The volcano is at Alert Level III (second-highest on Indonesia's four-level scale) ; Over 300 flights were affected, with airports in Jakarta, Bandung, and Lampung disrupted ; Authorities established a 3-kilometer exclusion zone around the active crater ; Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency plans cloud seeding to encourage rainfall that may help remove ash from affected areas

item.title: New Maps Show How Israel Has Thwarted Hopes for a Palestinian State
item.description: Ten years after maps of Israeli settlements shocked President Obama, updated 2026 maps show that settlement expansion has confined Palestinians to just 8% of the land, rendering the two-state solution virtually impossible. — Key takeaways: Over 500,000 Jewish settlers now live among 3 million Palestinians in the West Bank ; Since 2023, Israel approved 104 new settlements, up from just 3 during the entire Obama Administration ; Settler attacks documented by the UN surged from 107 in 2016 to over 5,300 since 2023 — more than 4 per day ; Palestinians now control approximately 8% of the land between the Jordan River and Mediterranean Sea; Israel controls 92% ; Netanyahu campaigns on never allowing a Palestinian state, while far-right Cabinet members suggest driving Palestinians out of Gaza

item.title: Google Maps Switches to "Lake America" as Canada Compares Change to SNL Skit
item.description: As Google Maps implements the "Lake America" name change following Trump's executive order, MapQuest refuses and surges in popularity while Canada's Ontario Premier Doug Ford calls the change "completely absurd." — Key takeaways: Google Maps now shows "Lake America" on mobile and desktop for US users, while Apple Maps initially kept "Lake Ontario" ; MapQuest publicly refused the name change and its tweet went viral, boosting the app to #1 on the US App Store ; "Lake America" appeared on Ontario government agency websites pulling data from Google Maps, despite Google saying Canadian users would see "Lake Ontario" ; Ontario Premier Doug Ford compared the change to a "Saturday Night Live" skit and installed a "Lake Ontario, today and forever" sign ; Google's region-localization means developers embedding Maps can set a Canada region to display "Lake Ontario"

item.title: 3 Hidden Google Maps Settings You Should Turn Off Right Away
item.description: Android Police identifies three Google Maps settings — background location tracking, automatic offline map downloads over cellular, and personalized ads based on visual search — that users should disable for privacy, battery life, and data conservation. — Key takeaways: Background location/Timeline tracking logs every location visited, duration, and route, and is enabled by default ; Automatic offline map downloads over cellular data drain battery, fill storage, and consume mobile data unnecessarily ; Google Maps serves personalized ads based on location, search history, and visual searches, pulling data from YouTube and Search ; Timeline tracking can be set to auto-delete after 3 months as a compromise ; Offline map downloads should be restricted to Wi-Fi only via Settings > Offline Maps > gear icon

item.title: UN General Assembly Endorses New World Map Showing Africa's True Size
item.description: The UN General Assembly endorsed the Equal Earth projection by 164-1, encouraging governments and institutions worldwide to replace the Mercator map that has distorted Africa's size for over four centuries. — Key takeaways: 164 member states voted in favor, only the US voted against, and 6 countries abstained ; The resolution encourages replacing the Mercator projection with Equal Earth but does not ban Mercator or impose a replacement ; Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland, but Mercator makes them appear similar in size ; French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called the correction "an act of truth" ; Advocacy group Africa No Filter wants accurate maps in schools, textbooks, newsrooms, and digital platforms

item.title: Google Maps Bluetooth Beacons Bring Precise Navigation to Tunnels
item.description: Google Maps now uses Bluetooth beacons installed in tunnels to maintain navigation continuity when GPS signals drop, an Android-only feature that Waze has offered for years. — Key takeaways: Google Maps uses Bluetooth beacons installed in tunnels to maintain navigation when GPS signal is lost ; The feature is activated via Settings > Navigation > Driving options > "Tunnel Bluetooth beacon" ; Currently Android-only because Apple limits background Bluetooth usage on iPhone ; Waze has offered a similar beacon-based tunnel navigation service for several years ; The feature provides real-time positioning information inside tunnels where GPS is unavailable

item.title: Can You Guess the Real Size of Each Country on the New World Map?
item.description: Al Jazeera launched an interactive map quiz that lets users guess which country is bigger, then morphs the map from Mercator to Equal Earth to reveal how distortion has been shrinking Africa and other equatorial regions for centuries. — Key takeaways: The interactive quiz lets users pick which country is bigger, then morphs from Mercator to Equal Earth to show the true proportions ; On a Mercator map, Greenland appears roughly the size of Africa, which is actually 14 times larger ; The distortion inflates Europe, Russia, and North America while shrinking Africa, Latin America, and South Asia ; The US called the resolution a "radical ideological project" and voted alone against it ; Togo plans a meeting in Lomé early next year with UNESCO, the African Union, and tech companies including Google to discuss implementation

item.title: How the GNIS Lake Ontario/Lake America Name Change Will Appear in Google Maps
item.description: Google's official blog explains that Maps will show "Lake America" to US users, "Lake Ontario" to Canadian users, and both names to everyone else, following the GNIS name change under Trump's executive order. — Key takeaways: The US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) formally changed "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States ; Google Maps follows official government sources (GNIS for the US) for name changes ; US users see "Lake America," Canadian users see "Lake Ontario," and users outside both countries see both names ; The update follows Google's long-standing policy for bodies of water with country-specific names ; Changes were rolling out as of August 30, 2026

item.title: Apple Maps Now Shows Ads You Cannot Turn Off
item.description: Apple has begun showing permanent, non-removable ads in Apple Maps for users in the US and Canada, with no opt-out setting — even for paying Apple One subscribers. — Key takeaways: Apple Maps now displays permanent ads on the main search screen and in search results for US and Canadian users ; There is no setting to turn off the ads, and even Apple One subscribers will see them ; Apple claims the ads are privacy-preserving, using on-device data not shared with advertisers ; The ads follow Apple's existing ad model in App Store, Apple News, and Apple TV ; Apple plans to expand the ads to the rest of North America soon

item.title: Why the UN's New World Map Won't Change Google Maps Anytime Soon
item.description: The UN's adoption of the Equal Earth projection resolution won't change Google Maps because the app's tiling system depends on Mercator's angle-preserving properties, and the resolution is nonbinding. — Key takeaways: The UN resolution passed with 164 votes in favour, 1 against (US), and 6 abstentions, but is nonbinding ; France announced it will switch official maps from Mercator to Eckert IV projection ; Google Maps uses a square-tile system since 2005 that requires Mercator's angle-preserving properties at all zoom levels ; Equal Earth and Eckert IV preserve surface areas but sacrifice angular accuracy, making them incompatible with current tile-based mapping infrastructure ; Togo plans to meet with Google, the African Union, and UNESCO within six months to discuss practical implementation

item.title: GIS Maps to Be Attached to Sale Deeds from October in Maharashtra
item.description: Maharashtra will attach GIS maps to property sale deeds starting October 2026, replacing decades-old boundary descriptions with precise digital maps in an initial 10-district rollout. — Key takeaways: GIS-linked sale deeds will replace textual boundary descriptions in Maharashtra ; Initial rollout covers 10 districts, with statewide expansion to follow ; The system integrates land records, building footprints, and satellite imagery ; The 'mojini' (land measurement) system will be implemented before registration ; Benefits include precise identification, fewer boundary disputes, and fraud deterrence

item.title: What Different World Maps Get Right — and What They Get Wrong
item.description: The BBC provides a comparative analysis of the world's most prominent map projections — Mercator, Equal Earth, and Peters — explaining the trade-offs between area accuracy, shape fidelity, and navigational utility. — Key takeaways: No flat map can perfectly represent a spherical Earth; every projection sacrifices something ; Mercator preserves compass bearings but massively distorts area, making Africa look Greenland-sized ; Equal Earth, adopted by the UN, preserves area accuracy but cannot be used for navigation ; The Peters projection (1973) also preserves area but severely distorts shapes of landmasses ; Critics argue Mercator's distortions have psychological effects, shaping how regions are perceived politically and economically

item.title: UN Tells the World: Stop Making Africa Look Small
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly to adopt the "Correct the Map" resolution, urging governments, schools, and tech companies to stop using maps that make Africa look smaller than it is. — Key takeaways: The resolution passed with 164 votes in favour, 1 against (United States), and 6 abstentions ; The vote encourages governments, schools, and tech companies to adopt equal-area map projections ; Togo spearheaded the resolution on behalf of the African Union ; Togo announced it would change maps in schools starting this year ; The resolution is nonbinding but carries significant symbolic and practical weight

item.title: Kan TomTom Terugkeren Naar de Hoogtijdagen van de Jaren Nul?
item.description: BNR Nieuwsradio examines whether TomTom can return to its golden years by pivoting from failed consumer products to enterprise and government clients. — Key takeaways: TomTom has shifted focus from consumer products to enterprise and government clients ; The company has had a string of failed consumer product launches ; The B2B pivot raises questions about whether TomTom can match its peak performance ; The article examines TomTom's strategic transformation and market positioning ; TomTom's map data and location intelligence remain core assets

item.title: Waze contre Google Maps : 4 Points Forts de Waze
item.description: Despite Google owning Waze for over a decade, the community-driven navigation app still outperforms Google Maps in four key areas: real-time incident reporting, volunteer-managed local data, EV charging routing, and speed camera alerts. — Key takeaways: Waze's community-driven incident reporting remains superior to Google Maps ; Volunteer contributors update local data that algorithms cannot capture ; Waze offers EV-specific connector type and charging network preferences ; Google Maps excels at finding businesses, reviews, and offline resources ; The two platforms have not merged despite a decade of shared ownership

item.title: UN to Vote on Adopting New World Map That Shows Africa's True Scale
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted on a Togo-sponsored resolution to phase out the Mercator projection in favour of the Equal Earth map, which accurately depicts Africa's true size relative to other continents. — Key takeaways: Togo's foreign minister Robert Dussey sponsored the resolution on behalf of the African Union's 55 member states ; The Mercator projection, created in 1569, makes Africa appear similar in size to Greenland despite being 14 times larger ; The campaign promotes the 2018 Equal Earth projection as a more accurate alternative ; Critics call the Mercator distortion "cartographic colonialism" for visually diminishing the global south ; The resolution is nonbinding but could influence classroom curricula and technology platforms

item.title: France Adopts Fairer World Map Ahead of UN Vote on More Balanced Geography
item.description: France officially abandoned the Mercator projection in its diplomatic representations, adopting the Eckert IV projection ahead of the UN vote on the "Correct the Map" resolution. — Key takeaways: France dropped Mercator in favour of the Eckert IV projection for official world maps ; French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced the change at La Fabrique de la Diplomatie ; France, the US, and Russia will appear noticeably smaller on the new maps ; The shift is both symbolic and geopolitical, reflecting France's support for the African-led initiative ; Barrot framed the change as both accurate representation and narrative shaping

item.title: Google Maps et Gemini Déploient une Nouvelle Météo Surpuissante
item.description: Google launched WeatherNext 3, an AI-powered meteorological model from DeepMind that integrates real-time satellite observations to deliver precipitation forecasts up to 50% more accurate, with hourly updates and 5km spatial resolution. — Key takeaways: WeatherNext 3 is Google DeepMind's latest AI weather prediction model ; Forecasts update every hour (vs. 6-hour lag in WeatherNext 2) ; Spatial resolution improved from 25km to 5km ; Precipitation forecasts are up to 50% more accurate ; The model integrates directly with Google Maps and Gemini

item.title: UN Approves Resolution in Support of Map That Shows Africa's True Size
item.description: Reuters confirms the UN General Assembly approved the "Correct the Map" resolution, with Togo leading the initiative and announcing immediate changes to school maps. — Key takeaways: The resolution was adopted with 164 votes in favour, 1 against, and 6 abstentions ; Togo led the UN initiative as part of the African Union campaign ; The 16th-century Mercator map diminishes Africa's size; the Equal Earth projection corrects this ; Togo's minister announced the country would change school maps this year ; The vote was largely symbolic but could influence global mapping standards

item.title: Mapping Precision: GPT Image 2.5 Solves Spatial Data
item.description: A new generative AI image engine called GPT Image 2.5 claims to solve the problem of producing spatially coherent cartographic visualizations, implementing topological constraint networks to prevent the geographic hallucinations typical of standard diffusion models. — Key takeaways: Standard AI image generators produce "geographic hallucinations" — rivers flowing uphill, disproportionate buildings ; GPT Image 2.5 implements elevation-aware topological constraints for spatial coherence ; Key features include hydrological gravity alignment, infrastructure network continuity, and orthographic perspective ; The engine resolves "texture bleed" where land cover classifications blur together ; Solar angle modeling is calibrated by latitude, season, and time of day

item.title: Warum Man in Simmerath Dem Navi Nicht Trauen Soll
item.description: The small German municipality of Simmerath has erected official signs telling drivers to ignore their GPS navigation systems, highlighting the tension between algorithmic routing and local traffic management. — Key takeaways: Simmerath erected blue-arrow signs telling drivers to turn off navigation apps ; Apple, Google, TomTom and other nav systems route through quiet residential areas ; The issue affects a new housing development (Meisenbruch) with ~90 plots ; Heavy construction traffic is being directed through residential streets ; Local officials want drivers to use higher-classified roads (L266, L246) instead

item.title: The Agent Drafts, a Human Approves: Inside State of the Map US 2026
item.description: State of the Map US 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin revealed three trends reshaping geospatial engineering: serverless map stacks replacing databases and tile servers with columnar files on object storage, AI agents drafting map data at industrial volume, and the deliberate human curation of sidewalk-level map data. — Key takeaways: Serverless map pipelines are shedding traditional databases and tile servers in favor of columnar files on object storage with parallel build steps ; AI agents are now drafting map data at industrial volume — from dashcam detections and satellite-derived geometry to automated validation of OSM contributions ; Sean Gorman's talk proposed restructuring OpenStreetMap tiles for AI consumption: embeddings, not pixels, as models now consume maps alongside humans ; Jeremy Herzog demonstrated restructuring the HIFLD critical infrastructure dataset for AI system consumption ("How We Prepared HIFLD for the Singularity") ; Sidewalks, crossings, and curbs — the fastest-growing part of the map — remain hand-drawn by the community, a deliberate choice the OSM community defends ; The guiding principle across all three trends: "the agent drafts, a human approves" — AI proposes, humans curate

item.title: TomTom Sees Breakthrough in Autonomous Driving Accelerating
item.description: TomTom expects partially self-driving cars to break through rapidly, predicting that by 2030 approximately 60% of new cars sold in Europe will feature systems capable of largely autonomous steering, acceleration, and braking on highways. — Key takeaways: TomTom predicts ~60% of new European cars sold by 2030 will have systems enabling largely autonomous driving on highways ; CEO Mike Schoofs sees 2026 as a transition year before revenue growth resumes, driven by automotive sector demand ; The company positions its map data and real-time traffic information as essential infrastructure for autonomous driving systems ; The prediction aligns with TomTom's CES 2026 focus on "mapping the road to autonomy" and powering the next era of driving ; TomTom's automotive navigation now combines predictive logic, a proactive AI agent, and integrated EV routing

item.title: Punjab to Digitise Property Records Through Drone Surveys and GIS Mapping
item.description: Punjab is launching a pilot project to digitise property records in 50 urban villages using drone surveys and GIS mapping technology to create accurate, transparent, and geo-referenced property documentation. — The Indian state of Punjab is embarking on a significant property record digitisation initiative, targeting 50 urban villages in a pilot project that leverages drone surveys and GIS technology. The project aims to create accurate, transparent, and geo-referenced property records that improve propert...

item.title: Apple Maps Renames Lake Ontario as "Lake America" After Trump Order
item.description: Apple Maps followed Google Maps in renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for US users after a Trump executive order, while MapQuest refused and Canada pushed back — highlighting how mapping platforms have become geopolitical instruments. — Key takeaways: Apple Maps renamed Lake Ontario to "Lake America" on its web version following a Trump executive order, days after Google made the same change ; Not all map providers complied: MapQuest explicitly refused to rename the lake and saw downloads surge 128% as a result ; Canadian government websites using Google Maps data inadvertently displayed "Lake America" and had to correct their maps back to "lac Ontario" ; The Globe and Mail published an opinion piece calling Google Maps "a tool of digital imperialism" ; Quebec government sites (Quebec511, SAQ, SQDC) and Ontario agencies (Metrolinx, HydroOne, LCBO) were all affected by third-party mapping dependencies

item.title: Google Maps on Android Auto Tests Darker Theme to Reduce Night Glare
item.description: Google is testing a darker interface for Google Maps on Android Auto in beta version 17.6.663424, aiming to reduce screen glare and driver eye strain during night driving. — Google is currently testing a darker theme for Google Maps on Android Auto, available in the beta version 17.6.663424. The update addresses a well-known problem: standard dark mode on navigation apps can still produce too much light at night, causing glare that distracts drivers and reduces visibili...

item.title: Google Maps Has Become a Tool of Digital Imperialism
item.description: The Globe and Mail argues that Google Maps' compliance with Trump's Lake Ontario renaming order exemplifies how dominant mapping platforms have become instruments of digital imperialism, shaping how millions perceive geography. — The Globe and Mail's opinion piece frames the Lake Ontario renaming controversy as symptomatic of a broader issue: the concentration of mapping power in the hands of a few technology giants who can be influenced by political pressure from individual governments. Two decades after Yahoo Maps shut dow...

item.title: Why Ford Chose Apple Maps Over Google Maps for Its New EV Platform
item.description: Ford chose Apple Maps over Google Maps for its upcoming universal EV platform (Fathom) because Apple offered better integration with vehicle systems for range estimation, charging, and battery preconditioning. — Key takeaways: Ford selected Apple Maps for its universal EV platform, with the first model called Fathom ; Alan Clarke, Ford's VP of advanced vehicle projects, cited Apple Maps' constant improvements and engineering team flexibility as key factors ; EV navigation requires deep integration with powertrain systems: range estimation, real-time charging station availability, battery preconditioning ; Apple's ability to cross-reference navigation data with topography and weather for dynamic consumption predictions was decisive ; This is native integration, not CarPlay Ultra — Apple Maps runs on Ford's own operating system

item.title: Cities Are Giving Their AI Chatbots a New Dimension: Geography
item.description: Maricopa County and Washington D.C. are connecting AI chatbots to GIS systems, enabling residents to ask location-based questions like "What construction projects are within a mile of my house?" or "Is my property in a flood zone?" — Key takeaways: Maricopa County launched Mari (public) and Marco (internal) AI agents built on IBM Watson with Esri GIS tools ; The system uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for text search and Esri tools for spatial queries ; After testing 11,000 prompts, the system launched in June 2026 and averages 706 users per month with 12,000+ questions asked ; "Nearest neighbor" searches convert user addresses to map points and calculate distances to relevant services ; Privacy safeguards include policy warnings, access controls, 13-month retention limits, and guardrails against legal advice

item.title: MapQuest Refuses to Rename Lake Ontario, Sees Downloads Surge
item.description: MapQuest's refusal to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America" following Trump's executive order propelled it to the top of the US App Store navigation category, with downloads surging 10x above normal levels. — Key takeaways: MapQuest reached #1 in free navigation apps on the US App Store, with usage multiplied 50x compared to a normal week ; Sensor Tower estimates 184,000 global downloads for the week of August 24, including 162,000 in the US — 10x the usual volume ; Daily US downloads jumped 128% between August 26-30, and MapQuest also reached #1 in Canada ; MapQuest adopted the same approach as with the Gulf of Mexico renaming, which it also refused to implement ; The service, launched in 1996, was acquired by System1 in 2019 after passing through AOL and Verizon

item.title: AMC Approves Citywide GIS Mapping and Digital Door IDs for Ahmedabad
item.description: The Amdavad Municipal Corporation approved a citywide GIS project covering 625 sq km with aerial LiDAR, 5,200 km of road surveys, 2.5 million geo-coded properties with Digital Door IDs, and a 3D digital twin — one of India's most ambitious urban mapping initiatives. — Key takeaways: Aerial LiDAR and photography will cover the 625 sq km municipal area with 240 ground control points ; 5,200 km of roads surveyed with Mobile LiDAR and 360-degree imaging; underground utilities recorded for asset management ; 2.5 million properties geo-coded through door-to-door surveys with Digital Door IDs for property tax assessment ; 3D digital twin with Level of Detail 3 models for 500 key buildings ; 12 GIS-based applications for town planning, disaster management, health services, and a citizen geoportal

item.title: HERE and Esri Bring a New Chapter in Location Intelligence
item.description: HERE Technologies and Esri are deepening their two-decade partnership to make location data a first-class enterprise IT asset, with a new location reasoning layer that lets AI interpret geospatial data without expensive model retraining. — Key takeaways: HERE and Esri are expanding their partnership beyond API-delivered data to persistent location data accessible through ArcGIS visualization and analytics ; HERE argues location data deserves recognition as a distinct discipline within enterprise IT strategy, not just another dataset ; A new "location reasoning layer" acts as an intermediary allowing AI to interpret location data without requiring full model training ; The partnership aims to bring Esri's ArcGIS capabilities to non-GIS users working with traffic, EV charging, and autonomous vehicle data ; Early assumptions that knowledge graphs and vector queries would suffice for AI integration proved insufficient — AI hasn't been trained on geospatial services

item.title: Summer 2026: Why Traffic Was More Fluid on French Roads
item.description: TomTom traffic data reveals that French roads were significantly less congested during summer 2026 compared to 2025, with the maximum congestion peak dropping from 35.6% to 29.4% and the number of high-congestion days in Île-de-France halving from 20 to 10. — Key takeaways: Maximum congestion peak in France dropped to 29.4% on July 7, 2026, compared to 35.6% in summer 2025 ; France experienced zero days above 30% congestion in summer 2026, versus 7 days in summer 2025 ; Île-de-France saw congestion peaks above 40% drop from 20 days (2025) to 10 days (2026) — a 50% reduction ; Key factors: shorter summer holidays, better anticipation of departure times, and trips spread across the entire season ; Declining purchasing power in 2026 also contributed to fewer and shorter road trips ; Gasoline consumption dropped significantly in May 2026, reducing state tax revenue

item.title: Building AI-Powered GIS Applications: Key Technologies and Challenges
item.description: A technical overview of the key technologies — machine learning, computer vision, NLP, and cloud computing — needed to build AI-powered GIS applications that go beyond displaying analysis results to recognizing patterns and predicting future events. — Key takeaways: ML enables GIS to predict traffic congestion, identify flood-prone areas, and estimate agricultural yields from spatial patterns ; Computer vision processes satellite and aerial imagery for damage assessment, unauthorized building detection, and urban mapping ; NLP allows non-technical users to query GIS in natural language ("show me areas within 5 miles of a river with rapid urbanization in the last 10 years") ; Performance and scalability are critical: GIS apps work with satellite imagery, 3D models, and large geospatial datasets requiring cloud infrastructure ; AI automates routine GIS analyst tasks, freeing professionals for higher-value work

item.title: Tech for Earth: The Machine Builds Its Own Model of the Planet
item.description: Geoawesome reviews Google Research's new planetary prediction engine that takes a natural-language geospatial question and autonomously runs the entire modelling pipeline — from data discovery to model training — while Overture Maps data powers new early-access web maps. — Key takeaways: Google Research's engine goes from plain-English question to trained planetary model without human data engineering ; The system achieved 76.8% mean R² across 21 CDC health indicators vs. 60.0% for manual pipelines ; It correctly flagged 15 of 18 newly invaded health zones during a 2026 DRC ebolavirus outbreak ; Eight early-access web maps built from Overture Maps Foundation data are now available ; NISAR satellite radar archive opened to the public, enabling widespread InSAR monitoring

item.title: One Region. 40,000 Bus Stops. An OSM Map at Every One. — State of the Map 2026 × Paris
item.description: At State of the Map 2026 in Paris, T-Kartor and Jungle Bus present their massive OpenStreetMap-based project to produce and maintain location-specific area maps ("plans de proximité") for 35,000+ bus and tram stops across the Paris region — Europe's most extensive public transport network. — Key takeaways: T-Kartor, the Swedish cartographic agency behind Legible London, WalkNYC, and Toronto TO360, has partnered with Île-de-France Mobilités to create "plans de proximité" — stop-specific area maps for the entire Paris region ; The project covers approximately 35,000 individual bus and tram stops, each requiring a unique map with high quality and consistency standards ; OpenStreetMap data is the backbone: the process goes from editing OSM data to delivering print-ready files to transport operators, with dozens of intermediate steps ; Jungle Bus, a local OSM community organization, has been a key partner throughout the effort ; The talk at State of the Map 2026 covers the full production pipeline: context, build, deployment, maintenance, and lessons learned

item.title: 5 Google Maps Settings Drivers Should Enable
item.description: BGR highlights five key Google Maps settings drivers should enable to improve their navigation experience, including customising car profiles for EV owners, downloading offline maps, sharing ETAs, and enabling Gemini AI voice control. — Key takeaways: Drivers should customise their car profile (gas, diesel, hybrid, electric) so Google Maps can suggest the most efficient route and show EV charging options ; Offline maps are essential for areas with spotty cellular connectivity, roaming charges abroad, or during natural disasters that disrupt service ; Sharing ETAs with friends and family provides safety benefits during road trips ; Gemini AI integration enables hands-free voice control for adding stops, finding restaurants, and asking questions about the route ; The settings are accessible on both Android and iPhone through the Google Maps navigation menu

item.title: Summer 2026: Why Traffic Was More Fluid on French Roads
item.description: Le Parisien reports on exclusive TomTom data showing that summer 2026 was less congested on French roads than the previous year, with fewer traffic peaks despite the final back-to-school weekend being busy. — Key takeaways: TomTom's exclusive data reveals fewer traffic jam peaks during summer 2026 compared to summer 2025 ; TomTom's traffic analytics are increasingly embedded in car manufacturers' built-in navigation systems ; The data covers France's major holiday travel routes and provides comparative year-over-year congestion analysis ; Even the final weekend before the school year was expected to be busy, but the overall seasonal trend was smoother ; TomTom's data positions it as a key provider of traffic intelligence for both consumers and the automotive industry

item.title: You Can Now 'Ask Maps' For Hyper-Specific Travel Advice. But Should You?
item.description: Condé Nast Traveler tests Google's new Gemini-powered "Ask Maps" feature that lets travellers ask hyper-specific questions without leaving the Maps app, while exploring what we lose when AI replaces the spontaneity of asking locals for directions. — Key takeaways: Google's "Ask Maps" is a conversational AI feature powered by Gemini that lets users ask hyper-specific travel queries directly within Google Maps ; Users can ask questions like "My phone is dying—where can I charge it without waiting in a long line?" or "Is there a public tennis court with lights I can play at tonight?" ; The feature charts travel itineraries based on crowd-sourced rankings and efficient routes with waypoints matching specified preferences ; Experts warn that over-reliance on AI may erode the serendipity and human connection of traditional travel ; Travel industry professionals note AI can help you "get to the door" but cannot replace what happens once you walk through it

item.title: Copernicus Emergency Management Service Maps Flood Damages in Northern Nepal
item.description: The Copernicus Emergency Management Service activated its Rapid Mapping component to assess flood damage in northern Nepal after a glacier collapse triggered a devastating debris avalanche and flash flood on August 26, 2026. — Key takeaways: A high-altitude glacier partially collapsed on August 26, 2026, triggering an ice and rock avalanche that descended 1,200 metres into the Lhende River basin ; The Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) activated Rapid Mapping under activation EMSR927 to map flood extent and assess damage across four Areas of Interest ; CEMS analysis around the village of Syapru Besi identified more than 240 buildings destroyed and 32 damaged ; The event affected northern Nepal and Tibet, generating powerful flows of water, mud, and debris downstream ; The satellite-derived damage maps support emergency response and recovery planning

item.title: Lake Ontario to Lake America: Who Gets to Decide What Goes on Maps?
item.description: The Conversation examines the formal process behind geographic name changes in the United States, using Trump's renaming of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" as a case study in who gets to decide what appears on maps. — Key takeaways: President Trump signed an executive order on August 27, 2026, renaming Lake Ontario as "Lake America" amid an escalating trade war with Canada ; In the U.S., place names are standardised by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names, part of the USGS ; Renaming typically starts locally: state or county proposals work up through state authorities to the federal Board ; The Denali/Mount McKinley name change took 40 years due to congressional opposition from Ohio ; Trump's previous executive order asked the Board to "honor the contributions of visionary and patriotic Americans," changing its policies and procedures

item.title: 2026 Nepal Debris Avalanche and Flash Flood
item.description: The USGS Landslide Hazards program is documenting the 2026 Nepal debris avalanche and flash flood, a catastrophic event triggered by a glacier collapse along the Nepal-Tibet border. — Key takeaways: The USGS has classified the event as an active landslide hazard under its Landslide Hazards program ; The disaster involved a debris avalanche and subsequent flash flood affecting communities along the Nepal-China border ; USGS monitoring and documentation supports understanding of cascade hazards involving glacial collapse, avalanche, and flooding ; The event adds to the scientific record on high-altitude glacier hazards in the Himalayan region ; USGS resources include geologic maps, topographic maps, and volcanic maps relevant to hazard assessment

item.title: Maps Show How a Glacier Collapse Triggered Deadly Nepal Floods
item.description: NBC News uses maps and satellite imagery to trace the glacier collapse and floodwaters that devastated communities along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing over 380 people with hundreds more missing. — Key takeaways: Over 380 people have died and hundreds more are missing since catastrophic flash flooding tore through villages along the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, 2026 ; Over 600 foreigners are missing, including 65 Americans, according to the Nepal Tourism Board ; Maps and satellite imagery trace the glacier collapse and the path of floodwaters downstream ; The disaster affected remote mountain communities along the Nepal-China border ; The event represents one of the deadliest glacier-related disasters in recent Himalayan history

item.title: Waze and Google Maps No Longer Give the Fastest Routes in France
item.description: Presse-citron explains why Waze and Google Maps now prioritize ecological routes over fastest routes in France, following a government decree that mandates navigation apps to highlight the lowest-emission itineraries. — Key takeaways: French decree n° 2022-1199 obliges digital mobility platforms to prioritize routes with the lowest greenhouse gas emissions ; Both Waze and Google Maps now prominently feature ecological routes, which are often longer than the fastest alternatives ; On highways with speed limits of 110 km/h or above, apps must also propose an alternative with a 20 km/h speed reduction ; Users can still manually switch back to fastest routes via app settings, though many are unaware of the option ; The Île-de-France region previously negotiated with Google Maps before the Paris 2024 Olympics to favor alternative routes and reduce congestion

item.title: GIS-Based Application Launched for Rural Water Asset Management in Karnataka
item.description: Karnataka's RDPR Minister launched a GIS-based mobile and web application to geo-tag rural water supply assets, improve transparency, and prevent fraudulent billing across the state's more than 3 lakh rural water assets. — Key takeaways: Karnataka launched a GIS-based mobile and web app for scientific management of rural water assets ; The application will geo-tag rural water supply assets with up to 5-metre accuracy, recording their physical condition and maintenance status ; More than 70,000 assets have already been mapped and documented during the first phase of verification ; All 3 lakh rural water assets will be digitised by the end of September 2026 ; The app also directs officials to remove pump sets and electricity connections from non-functional borewells to eliminate unnecessary power bills

item.title: ¿Qué factores llevaron a que Arequipa tenga un mayor nivel de congestión vehicular que Lima?
item.description: TomTom's latest Traffic Index reveals that Arequipa, Peru's second-largest city, has surpassed Lima in congestion level at 69.5%, with drivers losing 154 hours per year in traffic — raising questions about urban planning in rapidly growing secondary cities. — Key takeaways: Arequipa ranks 8th globally in TomTom's Traffic Index with a 69.5% congestion level, higher than Lima's 69.3% ; Drivers in Arequipa lost an average of 154 hours in traffic during 2025 — equivalent to 6 days and 10 hours ; Arequipa's congestion worsened by 1.9 percentage points from 2024, while Lima's increased by 0.8 points ; Despite having less total time lost than Lima (154 vs 195 hours), Arequipa's congestion percentage is higher due to its smaller road network ; TomTom monitors traffic in 500 cities worldwide using anonymised GPS data from drivers across the complete road network

item.title: Nepal–Tibet Floods in Maps, Photos and Videos
item.description: A devastating flash flood triggered by a landslide on the Nepal–Tibet border has killed at least 168 people with over 1,300 missing, and ABC News uses maps, verified satellite imagery, and video footage to document the unfolding humanitarian disaster along the Trishuli River. — Key takeaways: A landslide approximately 12 miles northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border post triggered massive flash flooding in Nepal's Rasuwa district on August 27, 2026 ; At least 168 people confirmed dead and over 1,300 missing, including 65 American tourists and 39 Australians ; The US Geological Survey registered a 5.2-magnitude landslide event, initially misreported as a 4.4 earthquake ; Verified maps and satellite imagery show the path of destruction from the Gyirong border through Nepal's Nuwakot district ; The disaster highlights the critical role of crisis mapping and satellite verification in covering remote, rapidly evolving natural disasters

item.title: Updated India Climate Opinion Maps for 2026
item.description: Yale's updated India Climate Opinion Maps tool visualises climate change beliefs, risk perceptions, and policy support across 34 Indian states and 634 districts, revealing sharp north–south divides in personal experience and climate literacy despite overwhelming national concern. — Key takeaways: The interactive tool maps climate opinions across 34 of India's 36 states/UTs and 634 districts using 25,000+ survey responses (2022–2026) ; After hearing a definition of climate change, over 75% of Indians in every state think global warming is happening, with rates from 80% (Andhra Pradesh) to 92% (Delhi) ; A stark north–south divide exists: northern states report higher personal experience with heat waves and perceived harm, while central/eastern states show low climate literacy (fewer than 50% in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal understand global warming is human-caused) ; Despite regional differences, 94% of Indians support national programs to teach about global warming and train people for renewable energy jobs ; The estimates use multilevel regression with post-stratification (MRP) combined with demographic, geographic, and climate vulnerability data, accurate to approximately ±7 percentage points at state level

item.title: TomTom Expert: Robotaxi Rollout Reveals Challenge of London as a Testing Environment
item.description: TomTom traffic expert Andy Marchant says London's complex street layout and evolving infrastructure make it an exceptionally challenging environment for robotaxi deployment, with high-precision mapping and live traffic data forming core infrastructure for safe autonomous driving at scale. — Key takeaways: TomTom's Andy Marchant identifies London's narrow roads, changing speed limits, and evolving street layouts as key challenges for robotaxi rollout ; Regulatory frameworks, liability models, and operating standards are still catching up to autonomous vehicle technology ; High-precision mapping combined with live traffic and hazard information is "core infrastructure" for automated driving, working alongside vehicle cameras and radar ; Location intelligence provides context "beyond the immediate line of sight" of vehicle sensors, making robotaxis "street smart" ; The same mapping data will be critical for UK government and transport authorities to plan and govern safe, scalable robotaxi deployments

item.title: München: Landshuter Allee Sperrung und ihre Auswirkungen auf den Verkehr
item.description: TomTom traffic data analysis reveals how the closure of Munich's Landshuter Allee for road maintenance sends ripple effects through surrounding neighbourhoods, with congestion levels rising dramatically in Neuhausen, Schwabing-West, Moosach, and Milbertshofen. — Key takeaways: The Landshuter Allee, one of Munich's busiest roads with over 70,000 vehicles daily, was closed for maintenance in both directions on consecutive weekends ; TomTom compared traffic data from August 13–16 (no closure) with August 20–23 (northern carriageway closed) to measure impact ; Neuhausen-Nymphenburg was most affected, but Schwabing-West, Moosach, and Milbertshofen-Am Hart also saw significant congestion increases ; TomTom's "Congestion Level" metric quantifies how much travel times increase in affected neighbourhoods compared to baseline ; The analysis identifies which alternative routes absorbed the additional traffic, demonstrating the value of real-time traffic mapping for urban planning
